reproduction_target: A software-tool paper introducing Tangram 2, a Python framework with three modules (Tangram2-mapping: probabilistic scRNA-seq-to-spatial alignment with cell-level, cluster-level and integrated modes; Tangram2-CCC: a per-gene linear model that decomposes expression into baseline, cell-type and interaction-driven components, yielding 'interaction coefficients'; Tangram2-evalkit: synthetic-data generation and benchmarking). Verbatim Data Availability: 'No new primary human-subject data were collected. The dataset used to reproduce the figures and results in the paper can be found at: https://zenodo.org/records/17594748'. Verbatim Code Availability: 'The Tangram2 package as well as the code to reproduce the result in the manuscript can be found at https://github.com/Genentech/tangram2'. The reproduction target is therefore the full manuscript figure/result pipeline: synthetic-data generation with Tangram2-evalkit; deconvolution benchmarking against ten published tools (Cell2Location, RCTD, SpatialDWLS, Stereoscope, SPOTlight, STRIDE, Seurat, DeepTalk, DSTG, DestVI) using Li et al's benchmarking framework; mapping-accuracy benchmarking against random/argmax baselines by Jaccard score; Slide-tags semi-synthetic 'visification' validation; a co-culture ground-truth differential-expression validation (GSE135382) evaluated on mouse colon Visium+scRNA-seq; a human lymph-node B-cell-activation GO validation; an 864-dataset synthetic parameter sweep; and two applied case studies (TNBC/ER+ breast cancer, and cSCC with Kneedle gene selection, gseapy pathway enrichment and TCGA Kaplan-Meier survival analysis). All steps are computational; no new wet-lab data were generated (the co-culture experiment is a re-use of a published GEO dataset), so W = 0.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the Methods sections of the v3 JATS full text (Tangram2-mapping modes, Synthetic Data Generation, Deconvolution Evaluation, Additional Deconvolution Analysis, Evaluation of Mapping, Tangram2-CCC Method, Tangram2-CCC Analysis with its four sub-analyses, Performance evaluation in Synthetic Data, Tangram2 analysis of TNBC and ER+, Macrophage-Treg interaction and TSK analysis in cSCC) plus the Data Availability and Code Availability statements. 21 computational steps, no wet-lab steps (W = 0), so S = 21. Mapping (C15) and colocalization (C16) in the breast-cancer case study are kept separate because they consume different outputs and disclose different parameters; Kneedle selection (C19), gseapy enrichment (C20) and the TCGA survival analysis (C21) are kept separate because each names a distinct third-party package and only these three carry exact version pins in prose (kneed v.0.8.5, gseapy v.1.1.3, sksurv v.0.23.1). IMPORTANT SCORING NOTE on the version axis: the Methods prose pins NO version for the authors' own package, for Python/PyTorch, or for Scanpy. Version = 1 is nevertheless assigned to every step executed through the tangram2 package because the repository README prose (in scope at stage 1) instructs 'micromamba env create --file envs/{x}_environment.yml' and the repository root shows envs/linux_environment.yml, envs/macosx_environment.yml, reqs/requirements.txt and reqs/cuda-requirements.txt. That is an environment-closure CLAIM only; the yml contents were deliberately NOT opened (that is the stage-2 check), so those steps carry subflag 'lock-present-unexecuted' and version_subtier 'floating' (prose is floating; the claim is what lifts the axis to the stage-1 ceiling of 1). C2 (the ten-tool deconvolution benchmark) is the one step outside that environment: the ten third-party deconvolution tools are not covered by the tangram2 env, no version is stated for any of them, and both the datasets and the accuracy-scoring methodology are delegated to Li et al's benchmarking paper rather than restated or deposited here - hence data = 1, code = 1, version = 0, params = 1, verdict NI. A human re-adjudicator who holds that a README-declared conda env is worth 0 rather than 1 in the absence of any prose pin would flip 17 steps from RI to NI; the axis values are recorded so that re-adjudication is mechanical.

steps.label: Tangram2-evalkit synthetic data generation (base engine): user specifies n_spots, n_cells_per_spot, n_types_per_spot; per-spot cell and cell-type counts sampled from Poisson with those means (types clipped to [1, n_types]); cells drawn from a seed scRNA-seq dataset and summed per spot so that G = T^T S; 'multinomial noise' on raw counts with multiplier m_s (default 1) and noise level epsilon (default 0); spatial coherence imposed by PCA of the per-spot cell-type proportion matrix P into 2D followed by an Earth Mover's Distance transport plan that reorders spots

Deconvolution benchmark of Tangram2-mapping against ten published tools (Cell2Location, RCTD, SpatialDWLS, Stereoscope, SPOTlight, STRIDE, Seurat, DeepTalk, DSTG, DestVI) on published datasets: 'The datasets, benchmarking methodology, along with the accuracy score computation, have been developed by Li et al in their benchmarking paper. The benchmarking model generates a final accuracy score based on the ranking of four evaluation metrics: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC), Cosine Similarity (CS), Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE), and Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JS). The detailed information of the benchmarking method and dataset can be found in Li et al's paper.' No accession, no per-tool version, no per-tool parameter set is given in this paper

Deconvolution evaluation on Tangram2-evalkit simulated data under three scenarios (perfectly paired / paired / unpaired). TNBC scRNA-seq of a single patient (Patient A) randomly split into halves A_1 and A_sc_2; A_1 used to generate A_sc_1 and spatial A_sp; paired scenario deconvolves A_sp with A_sc_2, unpaired scenario deconvolves A_sp with a different TNBC patient X_sc; 'each spot contains up to 10 cells, with a maximum of three different cell types per spot'; evaluation focused on scenarios 2 and 3

Mapping-accuracy evaluation on perfectly-paired simulations seeded from the cSCC scRNA-seq, with noise parameters 'ranging from 0.0 to 1.0' and spot counts 'from 100 to 500'; two baselines: 'The random baseline: assigning each cell to a random spot; The argmax baseline: assigning cells to the spot with highest Pearson correlation of gene expression'; scored by Jaccard after assigning each cell to its highest-probability spot

Ablation study of the Tangram2-mapping objective (Supplementary Figure 2): 'ablation study on the new loss function shows that the Bhattacharyya distance improves the overall alignment score, while the spot-level aggregation improves the mapping robustness when low-quality genes are included'. The ablation configurations, the low-quality-gene injection procedure and the alignment-score definition are described only at figure level

Slide-tags semi-synthetic 'visification' and preprocessing: 25x25 regular grid over the spatial domain giving 625 grid points; cells within 50 units of a grid point assigned to that spot, unassigned cells removed; per-spot transcript sums taken as the spatial profile; feature removal of names starting 'MT-', 'MT', 'RP', 'RPS', 'LINC' and ending '.1'; scRNA-seq cells with <300 counts and genes with <10 counts removed; spatial cells with <100 counts and genes with <10 counts removed

Scanpy normalization and highly-variable-gene selection, given verbatim as 'sc.pp.normalize_total(..., 1e4) / sc.pp.log1p(...) / sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(..., n_top_genes=5000)'. No Scanpy version is stated anywhere in the paper

Tangram2 mapping run on the Slide-tags semi-synthetic pair to obtain the cell-to-location map T: 'Tangram2 was run on raw counts using the highly variable genes as training genes.' Which mapping mode (cell-level / cluster-level / integrated), the number of epochs, the learning rate and the regularization weights are not stated for this run

Tangram2-CCC model fit: adjacency A and effective-neighborhood W derived from T and the cell-type indicator D; expression normalized by per-cell count division, x1e4 scaling and log1p; per-gene normal-likelihood model with learnable (gamma, alpha, beta, sigma) fitted by MLE; PCA dimensionality reduction to F components with parameters projected back, 'F is user-defined (default: F = 500)'; 'For the parameter fitting we use Adams as an optimizer, with 1000 epochs and 0.01 learning rate unless otherwise stated'. No random seed or initialization scheme is reported

Slide-tags validation of interaction coefficients by proximal/distal expression contrast: per interaction A<-B, distance from each receiver cell to its nearest signaler computed in original spatial coordinates; proximal and distal receivers defined by the 25th and 75th quantiles of that distribution; for the top 10 genes of every non-self cell-type combination the difference in mean expression is counted; binomial test with N = 1560 = 13 cell types x 12 interactions x 10 genes under p = 0.5

Co-culture ground-truth differential expression on GSE135382 ('94 deposited experiments' of splenic CD11c+ DCs from C57BL/6 mice alone or co-cultured with OT-II CD4+ T cells after OVA loading and LPS activation): Scanpy 'sc.pp.normalize_total(..., target_sum=1e4)', 'sc.pp.log1p(...)', then 'sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(..., method=wilcoxon)'; genes with adjusted p <= 0.05 and positive log fold change retained, yielding 1317 ground-truth genes

Mouse colon validation: four Visium sections (1A_Hh, 2A_Hh, 3A_Hh, 4A_Hh) concatenated with one scRNA-seq dataset; mouse-specific feature removal ('mt-', 'Mt', 'ENSMUSG', 'rps', 'rpl', 'rp-', 'rp', 'Rik'); named cell-type relabelings collapsing four T-cell labels to CD4+ and four DC labels to DC; 'We ran Tangram2 and Tangram on the paired mouse colon data with default parameters'; AUROC/AUPRC over the gene intersection with the co-culture ground truth, ranked by log fold change, against a highly-variable-gene dispersion baseline computed across DCs. The 'default parameters' are not enumerated in prose

Human lymph-node B-cell-activation validation: one Visium section (dataset 'lymph vis') plus unpaired scRNA-seq of the same tissue (dataset 'lymph sc'), Donor A16, cell types from the 'Subset_Broad' annotation, same filtering/normalization/HVG procedure as C6-C7, 'Tangram were run with default settings'; three GO pathways GO:0042113 (B-cell activation, positive control), GO:0042110 (T-cell activation, negative control), GO:0012501 (programmed cell death, negative control), obtained with filters 'taxon_subset_closure_label: Homo sapiens', 'type: protein', 'annotation_class_list_label: {PATHWAY NAME}', 'downloaded on 09/20/2024'; genes ranked by absolute interaction coefficient for B_naive <- T_CD4+_TfH and scored by AUROC against a normalized-dispersion baseline

Synthetic-interaction parameter sweep: grid effect_direction {up, down} x signal_effect_scaling {1.5, 2, 4, 5} x signal_effect_base {0.5, 0.8, 0.95, 0.99} x n_spots {100, 250, 500} x effect_size {10, 25, 50}, 'three replicates per parameter combination using different random seeds, resulting in 864 datasets'; Tangram2 and Tangram2-CCC run 'with default settings'; AUROC computed on interaction coefficients treating injected effect genes as positives. The seeds themselves are not reported

Breast-cancer (TNBC and ER+) mapping: scRNA-seq and Visium of the same subtype mapped with Tangram2-mapping in integrated mode; 'Data normalization is first applied to the scRNA-seq, and then the top 100 marker genes from each cell type are combined and used as the training gene for Tangram2-mapping'. The marker-gene ranking method and the per-patient sample list are not stated in prose

Breast-cancer colocalization analysis: 'the colocalization relationship between cell types is calculated by obtaining the Pearson coefficient between the cell type composition at spot level. The colocalization heatmap (Figure 4A) is obtained by averaging the Pearson coefficient from each patient of the same cancer subtype. The cell types with overall compositions less than 0.05% are removed from the analysis'

TNBC immunosuppression readout: 'Tangram2-CCC is then applied to the TNBC dataset to study the immunosuppressive mechanisms in the tumor microenvironment. After obtaining the interaction coefficients, we extract and visualize the predefined gene list from the relevant cell types.' The predefined gene list and the cell-type pairs selected for display are not enumerated in prose

cSCC per-patient mapping and CCC: six patients (P2, P4, P5, P6, P9, P10) with two adjacent Visium sections for P4/P6 and three for P2/P5/P9/P10; gene exclusion of prefixes (mt, mir, ac0, linc, itgb, rps, rpl, rp), all numeric-suffix isoforms, and names containing 'orf' or '-as'; each patient's scRNA-seq mapped to that patient's combined Visium sections; interaction coefficients averaged across patients; colocalization by Pearson with the same <0.05% composition filter

Kneedle top-gene selection for the Mac <- Treg interaction, given verbatim with an exact package pin: 'kneed.KneeLocator(ranks, interaction_coefficient, S=5, curve="convex", direction="decreasing") from kneed v.0.8.5'

Pathway enrichment of the Mac <- Treg gene set (259 genes): 'In the pathway analysis we utilized gp.enrichr from the gseapy package (v.1.1.3) with gene_sets=MSigDB_Hallmark_2020'. The gene-set library is named but its release/date and the Enrichr service snapshot are not pinned; no background set or significance cutoff is stated

TCGA survival analysis: TCGA_lusc, TCGA_hnsc and TCGA_skcm PanCancer Atlas studies with z-score-normalized RNA-seq; Mac <- Treg signature scored with scanpy.tl.score_genes; patients split into 1st and 4th quartiles as low and high classes; 'Kaplan-Meier curves were generated with kaplan_meier_estimator (sksurv v.0.23.1) using OS_STATUS for event and OS_MONTHS for time, with log-rank tests to calculate p-values'. cBioPortal study pages are cited without a portal release or download date, and scanpy.tl.score_genes is used without stating ctrl_size, n_bins or random_state

headline.static_readiness: 0/21 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 20/21 (95%) steps reach the stage-1 ceiling RI; 1/21 (C2, the ten-tool deconvolution benchmark) stops at NI because its datasets, tool versions and accuracy-score implementation are all delegated to Li et al's benchmarking paper rather than restated or deposited here. No step can exceed RI at stage 1 by construction, and the binding constraint on going higher is entirely the version axis: the Methods prose pins no version for the authors' own tangram2 package, for Python, for PyTorch or for Scanpy, and only three third-party packages are pinned anywhere in the text (kneed v.0.8.5, gseapy v.1.1.3, sksurv v.0.23.1). What lifts the other steps to version = 1 is a CLAIM, not a verified artifact: the repository README prose says 'micromamba env create --file envs/{x}_environment.yml' and the repository root exposes envs/linux_environment.yml, envs/macosx_environment.yml, reqs/requirements.txt, reqs/cuda-requirements.txt. Whether those files constitute a statically-complete, resolvable environment lock (conda-lock-grade under rubric Delta-2/Delta-4) was deliberately NOT checked - that is the stage-2 test, and it is exactly why this paper is a stage-2 candidate (capture_claim = env_lock_claimed, on the positive gate). Data is the strongest axis: every dataset is public and directly addressable (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17594748 carrying an 11.26 GB tangram2_data.tar.gz reproduction bundle, GSE135382, GSE144240, Broad SCP2169, two CZI cellxgene datasets, a 10x Visium public dataset, a Sanger cell2location h5ad, and three cBioPortal PanCancer Atlas studies), and 'No new primary human-subject data were collected'. Code is also strong at prose level: the public repository ships figure-by-figure notebooks (analysis/notebooks/figure_notebooks: Figure2c_deconvolution_benchmark.ipynb, Figure2d_mapping.ipynb, figure3_coculture.ipynb, figure_3_slidetags.ipynb, figure4b_mapping.ipynb, figure4c_colocalization.ipynb, figure_4_tcga.ipynb, Figure_4e1.ipynb, Figure_4e_2-4.ipynb, figure5c.ipynb, Figure5b/5d/5e.ipynb, supp_bcell_activation.ipynb, supp_pathway_overlap.ipynb, supp_synthetic_data_generation.ipynb, supp_synthetic_evaluation.ipynb) plus a paper_analysis_notebooks directory. The residual risks a stage-2 pass must resolve are: (i) the environment yml files are unresolved claims, (ii) the repository is cited as a bare floating URL with no commit, release or archival DOI (only an unreferenced 'beta-v1' tag exists; there are zero GitHub releases), and (iii) no random seeds are reported for the stochastic Adam fits, the 864-dataset synthetic replicate generation, or the Tangram/Tangram2 mapping runs.
headline.coverage: 21 computational steps built from the v3 JATS full text (fetched 200 OK by unauthenticated curl from https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2025/12/02/2025.09.28.679077.source.xml, 236910 bytes; title-phrase check 'Tangram 2' present), covering all Methods subsections plus the Data Availability and Code Availability statements, and cross-read against the GitHub landing page and README prose. No wet-lab steps (W = 0): the paper states 'No new primary human-subject data were collected' and the co-culture experiment that supplies the ground truth is a re-use of the published GEO series GSE135382. Supplementary Figures 1-9 are referenced in the text but the supplementary PDF itself was not fetched at stage 1, so the ablation configurations (C5) and the predefined gene lists (C17) remain prose-only. The contents of envs/*.yml, reqs/*.txt and the analysis notebooks were NOT opened - reading them is the stage-2 test.

gaps.where: All 21 steps; acutely C7-C9, C12-C14 (Scanpy / Tangram2 / Tangram2-CCC runs)
gaps.missing: No version is pinned in the Methods prose for the authors' own tangram2 package, for Python, for PyTorch/CUDA, or for Scanpy - despite Scanpy calls being quoted verbatim at API level (sc.pp.normalize_total, sc.pp.log1p, sc.pp.highly_variable_genes, sc.tl.rank_genes_groups, scanpy.tl.score_genes) and despite the CCC fit being a GPU-capable Adam optimization. Only three exact pins exist in the whole paper (kneed v.0.8.5, gseapy v.1.1.3, sksurv v.0.23.1) and they sit in the cSCC subsection only. The repository README claims an environment via 'micromamba env create --file envs/{x}_environment.yml' with envs/linux_environment.yml and envs/macosx_environment.yml plus reqs/requirements.txt and reqs/cuda-requirements.txt, but at stage 1 this is an unverified claim: whether the yml pins exact builds, whether it resolves today, and whether it covers the CUDA path are all unknown. A conda environment.yml is in general weaker than a conda-lock/pixi.lock/image digest because it records constraints rather than a resolved solution.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved lock for each declared platform (conda-lock or pixi.lock with hashes, or a container image referenced by digest) rather than only a constraint yml; state the Python, PyTorch and Scanpy versions in Methods; and record which platform the published results were actually produced on.

gaps.where: Code Availability statement; all steps that execute repository code
gaps.missing: The repository is cited as a bare, floating URL - 'https://github.com/Genentech/tangram2' - with no commit SHA, no release tag and no archival DOI. The repository has zero GitHub releases; the only tag, 'beta-v1' (5991517170a8da14a1079271096207b8926b6530), is not referenced in the paper. The repository was created 2025-11-12, after the first preprint posting (2025-09-30), and was last pushed 2025-12-08, six days after the v3 posting, so the branch a reader clones today is not identifiable with the state that produced the figures. Separately, C2's execution code (running the ten third-party deconvolution tools and computing the PCC/CS/RMSE/JS ranking score) is not provided here at all; the paper points to Li et al's benchmarking paper instead.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite a specific tag or commit SHA in the Code Availability statement and mint a Zenodo/Software Heritage archive DOI for that exact state; add either the ten-tool benchmark driver or an explicit statement of which Li et al release and which per-tool versions/parameters were used.

gaps.where: C9 (Tangram2-CCC MLE fit), C8/C12/C15/C18 (Tangram/Tangram2 mapping runs), C14 (864-dataset synthetic sweep), C3/C4 (random spot assignment and random dataset splits), C21 (scanpy.tl.score_genes)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere in the paper. The mapping and CCC objectives are fitted with Adam ('1000 epochs and 0.01 learning rate') with no stated initialization or seed; the synthetic sweep says only 'three replicates per parameter combination using different random seeds, resulting in 864 datasets' without giving them; the deconvolution scenarios rest on a random half-split of Patient A's cells; the random baseline in C4 is by definition stochastic; scanpy.tl.score_genes samples a control gene set whose random_state is unstated. Reported point values (Jaccard scores, AUROC 0.74 / 0.75 / 0.64 / 0.56, the 657/1317 overlap with p < 0.01, the N = 1560 binomial test) are therefore not bit-reproducible from the prose alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the seed (or seed list) for every stochastic step in Methods and in the notebooks, and report whether the quoted metrics are single-run values or replicate means with dispersion.

gaps.where: C13 (Gene Ontology pathways), C20 (Enrichr / MSigDB_Hallmark_2020), C21 (cBioPortal TCGA PanCancer Atlas), C6/C12/C13/C15/C18 (portal-hosted expression datasets)
gaps.missing: External resources are addressed by name and location but not by release or checksum. Gene Ontology is pinned only by a download date ('downloaded on 09/20/2024') with no GO release identifier; gp.enrichr fetches 'MSigDB_Hallmark_2020' live from the Enrichr service, whose served content and the gseapy library index can change independently of the gene-set library name; the three cBioPortal studies (lusc/hnsc/skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018) are cited as portal summary pages with no portal release or download date; the CZI cellxgene datasets are cited by collection/dataset UUID without a census/dataset version; the 10x lymph-node Visium dataset is cited by product-page URL; the lymph-node scRNA-seq is a direct .h5ad object served from a lab-owned Sanger object store with no DOI and no checksum. Every one of these can drift without notice, and none is mirrored with a hash.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin each external resource by release identifier plus checksum (GO release date-stamped OBO file, an MSigDB Hallmark release rather than the live Enrichr endpoint, a cBioPortal study download archive, a cellxgene census/dataset version), or deposit the exact retrieved snapshots alongside the Zenodo reproduction bundle.

gaps.where: C2 (ten-tool benchmark), C5 (loss ablation), C8/C12/C13/C14 ('default parameters' / 'default settings'), C17 (predefined gene list), C15 (marker-gene ranking)
gaps.missing: Several steps are specified only by reference to defaults or to unlisted lists. 'We ran Tangram2 and Tangram on the paired mouse colon data with default parameters', 'Tangram were run with default settings' and 'we ran Tangram2 and Tangram2-CCC with default settings' do not say which mode was used or what the defaults are at the unpinned code version; the ablation configurations behind Supplementary Figure 2 are not enumerated; the 'predefined gene list' visualized for the TNBC immunosuppression figure and for the TSK analysis is never listed in the text; 'the top 100 marker genes from each cell type' does not state the ranking test used to obtain them; the ten benchmarked deconvolution tools are given no parameters at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Enumerate defaults inline (or cite the config file and the code version at which those defaults hold), list the ablation arms, and publish the predefined gene lists and marker-gene selection procedure as a supplementary table.

gaps.where: Data Availability statement; every step consuming the Zenodo bundle
gaps.missing: The reproduction dataset is a single 11.26 GB opaque archive - Zenodo record 17594748 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17594748, published 2025-11-12), file 'tangram2_data.tar.gz', 11263322677 bytes. Neither the paper nor the record description provides a per-file manifest, a mapping from archive contents to figures or notebooks, or per-file checksums, so a reader cannot tell which of the eleven cited public sources are already inside it, which are preprocessed intermediates and which must still be downloaded independently. The public sources are listed as bare URLs and dataset nicknames ('slide-tags', 'cell cultures', 'colon', 'lymph vis', 'lymph sc', 'cscc', 'breast') with only two being formal accessions (GSE135382, GSE144240); the breast dataset is narrowed by the parenthetical '(donor_id: CID4465)' but the TNBC/ER+ patient lists used in Figure 4 are not enumerated.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a file manifest with checksums for the Zenodo archive, state per figure which archive paths and which external accessions it consumes, and list the exact patient/sample identifiers used in each case study.
